identity.name: KILBURN ENGINEERING LTD.
identity.industry: Industrial Thermal Processing & Nuclear Grade Equipment

summary.oneLiner: Kilburn delivered strong FY26 consolidated growth (Revenue INR 629cr, +~50% YoY implied) with robust 25% EBITDA margins, though Q4 cash flow was temporarily negative due to lumpy dispatches (INR 130cr) and Middle East logistics delays. Guidance remains constructive for 20-25% revenue CAGR to reach INR 1,000cr by FY28, underpinned by a INR 4,000cr+ inquiry pipeline and near-term capacity expansions, despite near-term order finalization slippages.

one-line thesis: Kilburn delivered strong FY26 consolidated growth (Revenue INR 629cr, +~50% YoY implied) with robust 25% EBITDA margins, though Q4 cash flow was temporarily negative due to lumpy dispatches (INR 130cr) and Middle East logistics delays. Guidance remains constructive for 20-25% revenue CAGR to reach INR 1,000cr by FY28, underpinned by a INR 4,000cr+ inquiry pipeline and near-term capacity expansions, despite near-term order finalization slippages.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Standalone INR 448cr (FY26), Consolidated INR 629cr (FY26); EBITDA Margin: 25.13% Consolidated FY26 (Q4: 22.95%); PAT: Impacted by full tax regime adoption (no carry-forwards vs prior year) and one-off INR 2-3cr building demolition write-off; Order Book: INR 467cr (Group, end-Q4); Net Debt: Stable borrowings despite working capital spike, cash flow negative INR 17cr (standalone) due to receivables buildup.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 20-25% CAGR (Target INR 750-800cr for FY27); Margin: 20%+ (Management comfort zone 22-23%); Order Inflow: INR 800-1,000cr (FY27); Capex/Commissioning: INR 40cr total; Saravali (Kilburn) and Pune Phase 2 (M.E. Energy) expansions completing by end-Q2 FY27.
order book & pipeline: INR 467cr consolidated backlog; Inquiry pipeline >INR 4,000cr across fertilizer, nuclear, petrochem, steel; Expectation to close INR 450-500cr of new orders by end-Q2 FY27.
segment / subsidiary detail: Kilburn (Parent): Fertilizer (dryers), Nuclear (components), Petrochem (vapor recovery); M.E. Energy: Waste heat recovery (Steel/Ferrous Alloy focus, Cement early stage); Monga Strayfield: Textiles, Food Processing, Defrosting (RF dryers).
growth verticals / optionality: Nuclear sector re-entry (2 projects in pipeline, Kaiga); Export market expansion targeting 30-40% revenue mix (US, Europe, Far East); Cement sector breakthrough for WHRB systems.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margins pressured in Q4 by high subcontracting mix and freight costs for Moroccan order; Material cost inflation (steel) mitigated by immediate booking policy; Management clarifies no automatic cost pass-through, relying on hedging at order stage.
capex / expansion: INR 40cr planned for FY27; Focused on Saravali plant expansion and M.E. Energy Pune Phase 2; Completion expected by Sept/Oct 2026 to support FY28 volume targets.
capital allocation: No further equity dilution (all warrants converted); Debt levels stable despite working capital fluctuations; Cash flows expected to normalize in H1 FY27 as receivables (INR 50-60cr Moroccan, others) are collected.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tensions (Middle East/West Asia) causing logistics bottlenecks and order finalization delays (2-3 month shift); Working capital intensity (days increased to 184); Execution delays in nuclear vertical (12+ month cycles).
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural growth and margin sustainability (22-23%); Cautiously realistic about near-term geopolitical headwinds affecting dispatch timing; Emphasized 'high aspirations' but guided conservatively (20-25%) to manage expectations.
non-obvious takeaways: Significant portion of 'Other Income' is operating in nature (FX gains on exports) and should be mentally added to EBITDA for true margin assessment (~80% of other income); Q4 gross margin dip driven by specific high-subcontract jobs, not structural cost creep.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Logistics bottlenecks and delayed dispatches due to Middle East crisis impacting revenue recognition timing | Kilburn Engineering Ltd | beneficiary | High | Company has INR 4,000cr+ pipeline and capacity expansions coming online; delays are temporal (2-3 months) rather than demand destruction; strong pricing power maintains 25% margins despite chaos. |

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).
